title: Partner asset lighthouse acceptance checklist (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This working checklist is a lightweight preflight / acceptance ledger for partner marketplace assets. Goal is to reduce back-and-forth at final review by standardizing required fields, UX copy scaffolding, security gating, and minimal QA. Use this during publisher onboarding and before sending to legal/launch ops.

High-level acceptance rubric (quick):
- Green (go): all required fields present, images pass size/contrast checks, billing SKU mapped, security checklist cleared.
- Amber (needs remediation): minor copy/format issues, missing secondary screenshot, or billing notes pending.
- Red (blocker): data residency, PII, or unsupported integration modes flagged; must fix before publish.

Required metadata (hard blockers):
- Tile title (<= 60 chars) — clear product name + optional partner qualifier.
- Short tagline (<= 160 chars) — one-line outcome statement.
- Long description (<= 800 chars) — problem, capabilities, quick-start value.
- Category tags (min 2): e.g., "Inference", "Embeddings", "Security".
- Contact email + support SLA statement (trial vs paid).
- Billing SKU ID + pricing plan mapping (trial, monthly, enterprise).
- Data residency option flags (yes/no + available regions).
- Privacy/PII statement — do not claim logging-free unless verified.

Design & assets (technical):
- Logo: PNG (transparent), 1:1, 1024px recommended; provide vector (SVG) if available.
- Hero image or screenshot: 16:9 or 4:3, 1920px width ideal; include alt text.
- 2–3 annotated screenshots with callouts (upload originals and cropped versions).
- Accessibility check: color contrast passes WCAG AA for primary button and tile background.

Copy cookbook (suggested variants to speed approvals):
- Tile title (variants): "Redwood Dedicated + PartnerX Connector", "PartnerX Inference Connector for Redwood"
- Short tagline (variant A): "Deploy PartnerX models with Redwood's low-latency routing and cost controls."
- 200-char preview: "Connect PartnerX to Redwood to serve models with predictable latency, autoscaling, and per-route cost controls. Includes trial provisioning and sample prompts."
- 400–600 char blurb (long description): [provide partner-specific features, deployment modes, supported models, security controls, and quick-start steps].

Functional acceptance checklist (tests to run):
- Provisioning flow: create trial tenant -> select partner listing -> provision demo instance in sandbox region. Expected: token created, demo prompts run.
- Billing flow: assign trial SKU -> upgrade to paid SKU -> verify invoice/payment metadata surfaces in billing console.
- Region gating: attempt deployment in restricted region (if partner claims support) -> confirm deployment outcome and region tag.
- API contract: run 10 sample calls at seq len=512 -> verify response shape, streaming behavior, error modes.
- Rate-limit behavior: hit burst of 200 rps -> ensure graceful 429s and documented retry-after header.

Security & compliance quick gates (blocking):
- Verified data handling: does partner process or persist customer prompt text? (Yes/No + storage controls).
- PII: any sample data or demo prompts that include PII must be scrubbed or flagged.
- KMS/HSM integration: required for Private deployments — provide KMS config example.
- Audit log support: confirm event types emitted (provision, request, rollout).

Legal snippet & product copy guardrails (for legal review):
- Do not promise specific latency SLAs in listing copy (surface SLO ranges only: e.g., "sub-second to low-second depending on model/region").
- Do not claim regulatory compliance (HIPAA/SOC2) unless partner evidence attached.
- Include link to partner terms and Redwood data processing addendum if applicable.

Launch ops & rollout gating matrix:
- Must have all hard blockers resolved + screenshots + billing SKU -> schedule listing publish.
- Canary cohort: release to 5% of traffic for first 48h, monitor latency/error budget.
- Rollback plan: predefine fallback model variant and region if errors exceed threshold.

Sample snippet bank (quick copy to paste into listing):
- Feature bullets:
  • Low-latency inference with autoscaling and cost controls.
  • Pin model versions and roll out safely with canaries and automatic fallback.
  • Deploy via Hosted API, Dedicated pools, or Private VPC.

- CTA examples:
  • "Try in sandbox — 14-day trial (no credit card)"
  • "Request enterprise demo and custom pricing"

Open questions / TODO (internal):
- Confirm SKU mapping with finance: partner trials that convert to Redwood billed usage vs partner-managed billing (ticket: GT-4521).
- Do we need an additional architecture diagram for Private/on-prem flows? If yes, request from partner.
- Legal: sample DPA attached? If not, ask partner for DPA checklist.

Manual reviewer checklist (for reviewer to sign off):
- [ ] Title within char limits
- [ ] Tagline + long description drafted and copy-edited
- [ ] Images uploaded + alt text present
- [ ] Billing SKU visible in console + price bands mapped
- [ ] Security questions answered (data retention, PII, logs)
- [ ] QA runs completed (provisioning, API contract, billing)
- [ ] Legal link reviewed or DPA attached

Notes & process tips:
- Keep a single source of truth in the partner's folder: name assets with partner-YYYYMMDD to avoid stale images.
- Use this doc as the checklist during the partner kickoff and assign owners per row to avoid churn.
- If a partner claims unique performance numbers, ask for a small reproducible benchmark and validate on our infra (dev task).

Next steps (owner: Aisha):
1) Send checklist to partner with "must provide" items highlighted (logo, 2 screenshots, DPA).
2) Open a Jira onboarding epic and attach this doc.
3) Schedule 30-min preflight with partner + eng (include DevOncall).

Slack channel for launch coordination: #marketplace-launches (ping @ben, @maya).

End of doc — use freely as working draft. Update as we get pattern failures; this is intended to reduce back-and-forth for small partners while preserving legal/compliance guardrails.
